newsitem.title: SAUDI ARABIA: Saudi reviews bids for $2 bln Shuaiba power plant.
newsitem.headline: Saudi reviews bids for $2 bln Shuaiba power plant.

text.p: Saudi Arabia is reviewing bids for a huge new steam power plant to be built and operated by the private sector, a Saudi official said on Monday.
Chairman of the Saudi Consolidated Electric Company - East (SCECO-East) Feheid Fahad al-Shareef said bid documents for the Shuaiba plant had been opened two months ago.
"Envelopes have been opened two months ago. Now they are being studied," Shareef told Reuters, adding the plant planned by the SCECO-West would have capacity of 1,950 megawatts.
Previously, SCECO-West officials had said the plant's planned capacity was 1,750 megawatts.

If it goes ahead as scheduled, Shuaiba will be one of the first in the kingdom to be set up on the build-operate-transfer (BOT) basis, which relieves the government of the burden of financing large infrastructure projects needed to meet demand from a fast-growing population, industry executives say.
They estimate Shuaiba will cost around $2 billion.
The kingdom's four main electricity companies, including SCECO-East and West, are all majority owned by the government.

Shuaiba is part of an ambitious programme to raise the power capacity in the kingdom -- where the population is growing at 3.5-4.0 percent annually -- to over 60,000 megawatts in 25 years from around 19,000 megawatts now.

Shareef, who was speaking after SCECO-East signed a $500 million loan with banks for its $1.1 billion Ghazlan II power project in the eastern province, said Shuaiba would be run on a BOT basis for 20 years before being transferred to SCECO-West.
He did not say which companies had submitted bids for the Shuaiba plant nor when the project was likely to be awarded.
The plant has been planned since 1993 but delayed by a lack of internal financing amid Saudi Arabia's huge Gulf War debts and low oil prices until early 1996.

SCECO-West director general Bakr Khushaim said in December local and international firms bidding for the Shuaiba project for the first time had been asked to "tell us how private money could contribute in building such plants".
SCECO-West has said the main part of the contract was for the supply of five 350-megawatt steam turbines, a jetty and a residential compound. It also wants high-voltage overhead lines.
